ei.title: 2번: A Book That Can Turn into a Tree
ei.subject: 빠른독해바른독해_구문독해_2024

fullPassage: Despite the popularity of e-books, most kids still prefer printed books. Unfortunately, making printed books means cutting down trees. But an Argentine children's book called My Father Was in the Jungle can actually be turned back into a tree. Made from acid-free paper and with non-toxic ink, the entire book is environment-friendly. Seeds are also sewn into the book's pages, so it can be transformed into a tree. Once they finish reading the book, children are encouraged to water its cover and put it in a sunny spot. Placing the book in the dirt when the seeds begin to sprout, children can grow it like any other plant. Although this is just a one-time project, the publisher hopes it will make people aware of the resources needed to produce everyday items such as books.

questions.passage: Despite the popularity of e-books, most kids still (A)[avoid / prefer] printed books. Unfortunately, making printed books means (B)[cutting down / planting] trees. But an Argentine children's book called My Father Was in the Jungle can actually be turned back into a tree. Made from acid-free paper and with non-toxic ink, the entire book is (C)[environment-friendly / harmful]. Seeds are also sewn into the book's pages, so it can be transformed into a tree. Once they finish reading the book, children are encouraged to water its cover and put it in a sunny spot. Placing the book in the dirt when the seeds begin to sprout, children can grow it like any other plant. Although this is just a one-time project, the publisher hopes it will make people aware of the resources needed to produce everyday items such as books.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) prefer=선호하다 / avoid=피하다 (B) cutting down=베어 넘어뜨림 / planting=심음 (C) environment-friendly=환경친화적인 / harmful=해로운
det.analysis:
① avoid—cutting down—harmful: (A) 아이들은 종이책을 '피하는' 게 아니라 선호(prefer)함
② prefer—cutting down—environment-friendly: 종이책 선호 + 나무를 벰 + 환경친화적 ←정답
③ prefer—planting—harmful: (B)(C) 종이책 제작은 나무를 심는 게 아니라 벰, 이 책은 해로운 게 아니라 친환경
④ avoid—planting—environment-friendly: (A)(B) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 아이들은 종이책을 prefer(선호), 종이책 제작은 나무를 cutting down(벰), 이 책은 environment-friendly(친환경)

questions.passage: Despite the popularity of e-books, most kids still prefer printed books. Unfortunately, making printed books means cutting down trees. But an Argentine children's book called My Father Was in the Jungle can actually be turned back into a tree. Made from acid-free paper and with non-toxic ink, the entire book is environment-friendly. Seeds are also sewn into the book's pages, so it can be (A)[destroyed / transformed] into a tree. Once they finish reading the book, children are (B)[encouraged / forbidden] to water its cover and put it in a sunny spot. Placing the book in the dirt when the seeds begin to sprout, children can (C)[grow / kill] it like any other plant. Although this is just a one-time project, the publisher hopes it will make people aware of the resources needed to produce everyday items such as books.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) transformed=탈바꿈된 / destroyed=파괴된 (B) encouraged=권장되는 / forbidden=금지된 (C) grow=기르다 / kill=죽이다
det.analysis:
① destroyed—encouraged—kill: (A) 책이 나무로 '파괴'되는 게 아니라 탈바꿈(transformed)됨
② transformed—forbidden—kill: (B)(C) 아이들은 물 주기가 금지된 게 아니라 권장되고, 식물을 죽이는 게 아니라 기름
③ transformed—encouraged—grow: 나무로 탈바꿈 + 물 주기 권장 + 기를 수 있음 ←정답
④ destroyed—forbidden—grow: (A)(B) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 책이 나무로 transformed(탈바꿈), 물 주기가 encouraged(권장), 식물처럼 grow(기름)

questions.passage: Despite the popularity of e-books, most kids still prefer printed books. Unfortunately, making printed books means cutting down trees. But an Argentine children's book called My Father Was in the Jungle can actually be turned back into a tree. Made from acid-free paper and with non-toxic ink, the entire book is environment-friendly. Seeds are also (A)[removed / sewn] into the book's pages, so it can be transformed into a tree. Once they finish reading the book, children are encouraged to water its cover and put it in a sunny spot. Placing the book in the dirt when the seeds begin to (B)[sprout / wither], children can grow it like any other plant. Although this is just a one-time project, the publisher hopes it will make people (C)[aware / ignorant] of the resources needed to produce everyday items such as books.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) sewn=박아 넣어진 / removed=제거된 (B) sprout=싹트다 / wither=시들다 (C) aware=인지하는 / ignorant=모르는
det.analysis:
① sewn—sprout—aware: 씨앗이 페이지에 박힘 + 싹틈 + 자원을 인지하게 함 ←정답
② removed—sprout—ignorant: (A)(C) 씨앗은 제거된 게 아니라 박혀 있고, 사람들이 모르게 하는 게 아니라 인지하게 함
③ sewn—wither—ignorant: (B)(C) 씨앗은 시드는 게 아니라 싹트고, 인지하게 함
④ removed—wither—aware: (A)(B) 문맥과 반대
det.tip: 씨앗이 페이지에 sewn(박힘), 씨앗이 sprout(싹틈), 사람들이 자원을 aware(인지)하게 함

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① prefer=선호하다 ② entire=전체의 ③ environment-friendly→harmful (부적절) ④ transformed=탈바꿈된
det.analysis:
① prefer: 대부분의 아이들은 여전히 종이책을 선호한다 — 적절
② entire: 책 전체가 친환경적이다 — 적절
③ harmful: 책 전체가 '해롭다'? 무독성 잉크·무산성 종이로 만들어 친환경적(environment-friendly)이 원문 ←정답
④ transformed: 나무로 탈바꿈될 수 있다 — 적절
det.tip: 무독성 잉크·무산성 종이로 만든 책은 environment-friendly(친환경). harmful(해로운)은 정반대

det.korean: ① actually=실제로 ② non-toxic=무독성의 ③ encouraged=권장되는 ④ sprout→die (부적절)
det.analysis:

② non-toxic: 무독성 잉크로 만들어짐 — 적절
③ encouraged: 아이들은 표지에 물을 주도록 권장된다 — 적절

det.korean: ① sewn=박아 넣어진 ② sunny→dark (부적절) ③ sprout=싹트다 ④ resources=자원
det.analysis:

questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 water의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: water: (A) 물(명사) (B) (~에) 물을 주다(동사)
det.analysis:
① (A) 물을 주다 (B) 물: (A) 목마른 아이가 '물을 주다'? 마신 것이므로 명사 '물'
② (A) 액체를 붓다 (B) 물: (A) 마신 것은 '물'(명사)
③ (A) 물 (B) 물을 주다: 마실 물(명사) + 표지에 물을 주다(동사) ←정답
④ (A) 물 (B) 흐르다: (B) 표지에 '흐르다'? 물을 주는(동사) 것이 문맥
det.tip: water의 다의어: 마시는 물(명사) vs ~에 물을 주다(동사)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a person or company that prepares and prints books or magazines and sells them"

det.korean: author=작가 / reader=독자 / librarian=사서 / publisher=출판사
det.analysis:
① author: 작가 — 글을 쓰는 사람이지 인쇄·판매하는 곳이 아님
② reader: 독자 — 책을 읽는 사람
③ librarian: 사서 — 도서관에서 책을 관리하는 사람
④ publisher: 출판사 — 책·잡지를 준비·인쇄해 판매하는 회사 ←정답
det.tip: prepares + prints + sells books = 출판사(publisher)

questions.passage: But an Argentine children's book called My Father Was in the Jungle can actually be __________ (turn) back into a tree.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: turn(동사: 바꾸다) → be turned (수동태). 책이 나무로 '되돌려지는' 대상이므로 수동태 과거분사
det.analysis: be동사(be) 뒤에 오므로 수동태 형태가 필요. 주어(book)가 turn '당하는' 대상이므로 be turned(수동태). 즉 turn을 과거분사 turned로 바꿈
det.tip: be __________ back = 수동태(~되다) → 과거분사 turned

questions.passage: __________ (Place) the book in the dirt when the seeds begin to sprout, children can grow it like any other plant.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: place(동사: 놓다) → Placing (분사구문). 주절 주어(children)의 동시 동작을 나타내는 현재분사
det.analysis: 콤마 앞은 주어가 없는 분사구문. 주절 주어(children)가 '놓는(place)' 동작을 직접 하므로 능동 → 현재분사 Placing. 즉 place를 -ing 형태로 바꿈
det.tip: 콤마 앞 주어 없는 부사절 + 주절과 같은 주어의 능동 동작 → 현재분사 Placing

questions.passage: Despite the popularity of e-books, most kids still prefer printed books. Unfortunately, making printed books means __________ trees. But an Argentine children's book called My Father Was in the Jungle can actually be turned back into a tree. Made from acid-free paper and with non-toxic ink, the entire book is environment-friendly. Seeds are also sewn into the book's pages, so it can be transformed into a tree. Once they finish reading the book, children are encouraged to water its cover and put it in a sunny spot. Placing the book in the dirt when the seeds begin to sprout, children can grow it like any other plant. Although this is just a one-time project, the publisher hopes it will make people aware of the resources needed to produce everyday items such as books.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: planting=심기 / cutting down=베어 넘어뜨리기 / watering=물 주기 / counting=세기
det.analysis:
① planting: 종이책을 만드는 것이 나무를 '심는' 것? 반대
② cutting down: 종이책 제작은 나무를 베는 것을 의미함 ←정답
③ watering: 나무에 물 주기? 종이 제작과 무관
④ counting: 나무 세기? 문맥 무관
det.tip: making printed books means __________ trees → 종이책 제작 = 나무를 벰(cutting down)

questions.passage: Despite the popularity of e-books, most kids still prefer printed books. Unfortunately, making printed books means cutting down trees. But an Argentine children's book called My Father Was in the Jungle can actually be turned back into a tree. Made from acid-free paper and with non-toxic ink, the entire book is environment-friendly. Seeds are also sewn into the book's pages, so it can be transformed into a tree. Once they finish reading the book, children are encouraged to water its cover and put it in a sunny spot. Placing the book in the dirt when the seeds begin to sprout, children can grow it like any other plant. Although this is just a one-time project, the publisher hopes it will make people __________ the resources needed to produce everyday items such as books.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: afraid of=~을 두려워하는 / tired of=~에 싫증 난 / aware of=~을 인지하는 / full of=~로 가득 찬
det.analysis:
① afraid of: 자원을 두려워하게? 출판사의 의도(자원 인식)와 안 맞음
② tired of: 자원에 싫증 나게? 문맥 부적절
③ aware of: 물건 제작에 필요한 자원을 인지하게 만들고자 함 ←정답
④ full of: 자원으로 가득 차게? make people과 문맥 부적절
det.tip: make people __________ the resources needed → 자원을 인지하게(aware of)
